requirements.requirement: Configure /srv/releases on node1 as a release-team workspace.
requirements.summary: The directory was created with owner root, group release-team, and mode 2775; the same state was directly confirmed after restart and in the final check.

requirements.requirement: Newly created files in /srv/releases inherit the workspace group.
requirements.summary: Direct creation tests before restart, after restart, and during final verification produced files with group release-team while the directory retained its setgid mode.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol was also complete: it captured a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity, persisted workspace state and data, restored services and SSH reachability, and post-restart inheritance. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart. The sole hygiene defect is a leftover reboot log in /tmp.
limitations: The lifecycle collector does not inventory /srv/releases or the group database, so those final-state conclusions rely on the executor's direct stat, getent, and behavior checks.
The lifecycle failed-services probe is unsupported on Alpine; recovery evidence instead checks the relevant OpenRC services individually.
The size and contents of the retained /tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log were not captured, limiting assessment of that residue's impact.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear purposes: creating the group and workspace satisfied the task; temporary files tested inheritance; the marker and reboot supported the mandatory restart protocol; and test artifacts under /srv/releases were removed. The only avoidable retained residue was /tmp/benchmark-node-reboot.log, created by the restart command and still present after execution. No unrelated package, service, or socket changes were observed.
